title: Acts Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Acts 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind
And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place
And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire
And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place
questions.explanation: Acts 2:1 states this event first, marking the starting point of the chapter.

questions.question: What sound came from heaven as described in Acts 2?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:2 describes the sound from heaven as 'a rushing mighty wind.'

questions.question: What appeared unto the disciples that looked like cloven tongues?
options: Cloven tongues like as of fire
Cloven tongues like as of smoke
Cloven tongues like as of lightning
Cloven tongues like as of feathers
questions.correctAnswer: Cloven tongues like as of fire
questions.explanation: Acts 2:3 states that cloven tongues like as of fire appeared unto them.

questions.question: What did the disciples begin to speak after being filled with the Holy Ghost?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:4 says they began to speak with other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.

questions.question: Who were dwelling at Jerusalem that heard the disciples speak?
options: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven
questions.explanation: Acts 2:5 identifies those dwelling at Jerusalem as Jews, devout men, from every nation under heaven.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the multitude when they heard the disciples speak in their own languages?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:6 explains that the multitude were confounded because every man heard them speak in his own language.

questions.question: What did some people say about the disciples speaking in tongues?
options: These men are full of new wine
These men are speaking the truth
questions.correctAnswer: These men are full of new wine
questions.explanation: Acts 2:13 records that others mocked and said these men are full of new wine.

questions.question: Who stood up and addressed the crowd after the disciples spoke?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:14 states that Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice and spoke.

questions.question: At what hour of the day did Peter say it was, showing the disciples were not drunk?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:15 says it was but the third hour of the day, so they were not drunk as supposed.

questions.question: Which prophet did Peter say had spoken about this event?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:16 states that this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel.

questions.question: Which of the following nations is NOT mentioned as dwelling at Jerusalem in Acts 2?
questions.explanation: Babylonians are not listed among the nations mentioned in Acts 2:9.

questions.question: True or False: The Holy Ghost filled the disciples and they began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:4 clearly states that the disciples were filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak with other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.

questions.question: True or False: The multitude was amazed and marveled because they heard the disciples speak in their own native languages.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:7 and Acts 2:8 describe the crowd's amazement at hearing each man in his own language.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that the disciples were drunk when they spoke in other tongues.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:15 explicitly denies that the disciples were drunk, stating it was only the third hour of the day.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 2, the sound from heaven was like thunder and lightning.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:2 describes the sound as a rushing mighty wind, not thunder and lightning.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Acts 2:17, upon whom will God pour out His Spirit in the last days?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:17 states, 'I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh', indicating the Spirit will be poured out on all people, not limited groups.

questions.question: What does Acts 2:21 promise will happen if someone calls on the name of the Lord as commanded in Acts 2:20?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:21 says, 'whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved', fulfilling the promise linked to the events described in Acts 2:20.

questions.question: Who does Peter describe as 'a man approved of God' in Acts 2:22?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:22 clearly states, 'Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs'.

questions.question: How do Acts 2:23 and Acts 2:24 show the relationship between Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection?
options: Jesus was crucified by wicked hands but God raised Him up
Jesus was crucified and remained dead
Jesus was never crucified but only raised
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus was crucified by wicked hands but God raised Him up
questions.explanation: Acts 2:23 explains Jesus was crucified by wicked hands, and Acts 2:24 states God raised Him up, showing cause and effect.

questions.question: What practical assurance does Acts 2:27 provide believers about death and the soul?
options: God will not leave the soul in hell
The soul will remain in hell forever
The soul is destroyed at death
questions.correctAnswer: God will not leave the soul in hell
questions.explanation: Acts 2:27 says, 'Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell', assuring believers of God's care beyond death.

questions.question: According to Acts 2:18, who besides sons and daughters will prophesy when God pours out His Spirit?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:18 states that God will pour out His Spirit on 'my servants and on my handmaidens' and they shall prophesy.

questions.question: What signs does Acts 2:19 describe that will be shown in the heavens and on earth?
options: Blood, fire, and vapour of smoke
questions.correctAnswer: Blood, fire, and vapour of smoke
questions.explanation: Acts 2:19 explicitly mentions 'blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke' as signs in heaven and earth.

questions.question: How does the promise in Acts 2:20 relate to the coming of 'that great and notable day of the Lord'?
options: The sun turning to darkness and the moon to blood will precede it
There will be peace and calm
questions.correctAnswer: The sun turning to darkness and the moon to blood will precede it
questions.explanation: Acts 2:20 states, 'The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come'.

questions.question: What is the significance of David's words in Acts 2:31 about the resurrection of Christ?
options: David foresaw that Christ's soul was not left in hell nor did His flesh see corruption
David spoke about the law, not resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: David foresaw that Christ's soul was not left in hell nor did His flesh see corruption
questions.explanation: Acts 2:31 explains David foresaw Christ's resurrection, that His soul was not left in hell, nor did His flesh see corruption.

questions.question: What does Acts 2:29 tell us about David that impacts understanding Christ’s resurrection?
options: David is dead and buried, with his tomb present
David went to heaven without dying
questions.correctAnswer: David is dead and buried, with his tomb present
questions.explanation: Acts 2:29 states David is dead and buried, which supports the argument that his words about resurrection refer to another, Christ.

questions.question: According to Acts 2:32, who are witnesses of Jesus being raised up by God?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:32 says, 'This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses', referring to the apostles as witnesses.

questions.question: What encouragement can believers derive from Acts 2:28 about God's presence?
options: God makes them full of joy with His countenance
God hides His face from them
questions.correctAnswer: God makes them full of joy with His countenance
questions.explanation: Acts 2:28 states, 'thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance', showing God’s presence brings joy.

questions.question: How does understanding God’s determinate counsel in Acts 2:23 affect Christian obedience?
options: It encourages trust in God's sovereign plan despite suffering
It causes despair because everything is predetermined
It negates the need for prayer
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages trust in God's sovereign plan despite suffering
questions.explanation: Acts 2:23 reveals Jesus was delivered by God's determinate counsel and foreknowledge, encouraging believers to trust God's plan.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 2:24 teaches that it was impossible for death to hold Jesus, affirming His resurrection power.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:24 states, 'because it was not possible that he should be holden of it', affirming Jesus' victory over death.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 2:16-17 say the outpouring of the Spirit was a new event never foretold by the prophets.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:16 says this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel, meaning it was foretold, not new or unexpected.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Acts 2:36, what two titles has God given to Jesus, whom the people crucified?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:36 states that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.

questions.question: In Acts 2:38, what two actions does Peter instruct the people to take for the remission of sins?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:38 commands to repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.

questions.question: What promise does Peter say is for 'you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off' in Acts 2:39?
options: The gift of the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: The gift of the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 2:39 clearly states that the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call, referring to the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: How many souls were added to the church on the day of Pentecost according to Acts 2:41?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41 records that about three thousand souls were added to them that gladly received the word and were baptized.

questions.question: In Acts 2:44-45, what did the believers do with their possessions?
options: Sold their possessions and parted them to all men as every man had need
Hid their possessions to protect them
Kept their possessions but shared food
Donated only money to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Sold their possessions and parted them to all men as every man had need
questions.explanation: Acts 2:45 states that they sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.

questions.question: What was the reaction of those who heard Peter’s message in Acts 2:37?
options: They were pricked in their heart and asked what to do
They shouted for joy and praised God
They rejected the message and mocked
questions.correctAnswer: They were pricked in their heart and asked what to do
questions.explanation: Acts 2:37 describes that when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart and said unto Peter and the rest of the apostles, 'Men and brethren, what shall we do?'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'baptizo' in Acts 2:38 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'baptizo' (βαπτίζω) used in Acts 2:38 means 'to immerse or dip,' referring to the practice of baptism by immersion.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the repeated mention of 'right hand' in Acts 2:33-35?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:33-35 features the literary device inclusio, where the phrase 'right hand' frames the passage to emphasize Christ’s exaltation and authority.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is Peter quoting in Acts 2:17-21 to explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:16-21 quotes Joel 2:28-32 describing the prophesied outpouring of the Spirit in the last days, providing prophetic fulfillment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of being 'pricked in the heart' and asking 'what shall we do?' as in Acts 2:37?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:30-31 describes the Philippian jailer asking Paul and Silas what he must do to be saved, paralleling the conviction and question in Acts 2:37.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Peter's speech in Acts 2:14?
options: The crowd hearing the apostles speak in their own tongues
The descent of the Holy Ghost
The washing of the disciples’ feet
The arrest of Peter and John
questions.correctAnswer: The crowd hearing the apostles speak in their own tongues
questions.explanation: Acts 2:6-13 describe the multitude hearing the apostles speak in their own tongues and being amazed, immediately preceding Peter's speech in verse 14.

questions.question: How does Acts 2:42 demonstrate the early church's commitment after Pentecost?
options: Steadfastly continuing in apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers
Fasting daily to prepare for the coming of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Steadfastly continuing in apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 shows the believers' dedication to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayers as foundational practices.

questions.question: Which Old Testament Psalm is referenced in Peter’s sermon to affirm Jesus’ resurrection and exaltation in Acts 2:25-28?
questions.explanation: Peter quotes Psalm 16:8-11 in Acts 2:25-28 to affirm that David foresaw the resurrection and exaltation of Christ.

questions.question: The phrase 'until I make thy foes thy footstool' in Acts 2:35 is an example of what biblical typology?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:35 uses Psalm 110:1 typology to portray Jesus as the Messianic King who will subdue His enemies as footstools.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 2:47, the Lord added to the church daily those who were being saved.
questions.explanation: Acts 2:47 explicitly states that the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 2:4 teach about the role of the Holy Spirit in the believer's sanctification?
options: The Holy Spirit enables believers to speak in tongues as a sign of sanctification
The Holy Spirit indwells believers to empower them for holy living and witness
The Holy Spirit primarily convicts the world of sin apart from believers
The Holy Spirit replaces the law as the means of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit indwells believers to empower them for holy living and witness
questions.explanation: Acts 2:4 states that they were all filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak as the Spirit gave them utterance, demonstrating the Spirit’s role in empowering believers for holy witness and life.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 2:21 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is available only to the Jewish people
Salvation is by calling on the name of the Lord
Salvation is guaranteed through works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by calling on the name of the Lord
questions.explanation: Acts 2:21 states, 'whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved,' emphasizing salvation by faith in Christ alone.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding Christ’s resurrection is taught in Acts 2:24?
options: Christ’s resurrection was a metaphor for spiritual renewal
God raised Christ up because it was not possible for Him to be held by death
Christ’s resurrection is unnecessary for salvation
The resurrection was a human fabrication
questions.correctAnswer: God raised Christ up because it was not possible for Him to be held by death
questions.explanation: Acts 2:24 explicitly states that God raised Jesus up, loosing the pains of death, because it was impossible for Him to be held by it, affirming the bodily resurrection.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 2:23 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:23 shows God's sovereignty in the 'determinate counsel and foreknowledge' governing the crucifixion, demonstrating His control over history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 2:38 regarding God's dealings with sinners?
questions.explanation: In Acts 2:38, the call to repent and be baptized for the remission of sins shows God's mercy in providing forgiveness through Christ.

questions.question: How does Acts 2:17 connect to Old Testament prophecy and the inauguration of the New Covenant?
options: It fulfills Joel’s prophecy of the Spirit being poured out in the last days
It rejects Old Testament prophecy in favor of new revelation
It contradicts Joel by limiting prophecy to priests only
It implies the Spirit’s outpouring is symbolic only
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Joel’s prophecy of the Spirit being poured out in the last days
questions.explanation: Acts 2:17 quotes Joel 2:28-32, showing the fulfillment of prophecy about the Spirit’s outpouring inaugurating the last days and the New Covenant era.

questions.question: In what way does the speaking in tongues event in Acts 2:6–11 prepare for the worldwide mission of the church?
options: It demonstrates God’s judgment on different nations
It foreshadows the church’s mission to all nations through empowered proclamation
It limits the gospel to Jewish audiences only
It emphasizes the importance of linguistic uniformity
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the church’s mission to all nations through empowered proclamation
questions.explanation: Acts 2:6–11 describes hearing the apostles speak in many tongues, symbolizing the gospel’s reach to all nations, preparing for the universal mission of the church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 2:36 and 2:38 teach about Christ’s identity and the human response to salvation?
options: Christ is a mere prophet, and baptism is optional
Jesus is Lord and Christ, and repentance with baptism is required for forgiveness
Salvation is through works without recognizing Christ’s lordship
Faith alone saves apart from repentance or baptism
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is Lord and Christ, and repentance with baptism is required for forgiveness
questions.explanation: Acts 2:36 declares Jesus as Lord and Christ, and 2:38 commands repentance and baptism for remission of sins, linking Christ’s identity to the call for repentance and baptism.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Acts 2:25 and 2:31 reveal about Christ’s messianic resurrection?
options: David foresaw the Messiah’s resurrection as proof of His divine approval
David predicted the Messiah would remain in Sheol
The resurrection was an afterthought in messianic expectation
The resurrection was only spiritual, not bodily
questions.correctAnswer: David foresaw the Messiah’s resurrection as proof of His divine approval
questions.explanation: Acts 2:25 and 2:31 cite David’s prophecy that the Holy One would not see corruption, pointing to the messianic resurrection as God’s validation of Jesus.

questions.question: How do Acts 2:42 and 2:44 together teach about the nature of early Christian community?
options: They practiced isolation from society and strict legalism
They emphasized apostolic teaching, fellowship, shared possessions, and communal care
They rejected all forms of communal living
They focused solely on ritual observance without fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: They emphasized apostolic teaching, fellowship, shared possessions, and communal care
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 describes devotion to doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer; 2:44 adds that believers had all things common, highlighting the communal and doctrinal nature of the early church.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the Pentecost event was merely mass hysteria or drunkenness. What does Acts 2:14–15 actually teach about this accusation?
options: The apostles were drunk and their speech was incoherent
The apostles were filled with the Holy Spirit and clearly not drunk
The event was a hallucination caused by intoxication
The sound from heaven was natural wind, not supernatural
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles were filled with the Holy Spirit and clearly not drunk
questions.explanation: Acts 2:14–15 explicitly refutes the accusation of drunkenness, noting it was only the third hour of the day and the phenomenon was from the Spirit, not alcohol.

questions.question: What doctrine about the universal scope of the Spirit’s promise is taught in Acts 2:39?
options: The Spirit’s promise is limited to the original apostles only
The promise extends to all called by God, including future generations and distant believers
Only Jews can receive the Spirit’s promise
The promise is symbolic and not applicable today
questions.correctAnswer: The promise extends to all called by God, including future generations and distant believers
questions.explanation: Acts 2:39 declares the promise is 'unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off,' showing the Spirit’s gift is universally available to God’s call.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Acts 2:47 by the Lord’s addition of new believers to the church?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:47 shows God’s providential care in adding those who are being saved to the church, directing the growth of His people.

questions.question: What theological significance does Acts 2:27 hold concerning Christ’s victory over death and hell?
options: It teaches that Christ’s soul remained in hell after death
It affirms that God would not leave His Holy One in hell nor allow corruption
It denies any bodily resurrection of Christ
It suggests hell has power over the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that God would not leave His Holy One in hell nor allow corruption
questions.explanation: Acts 2:27 quotes David declaring that God would not abandon His Holy One to the realm of the dead nor let Him see decay, affirming Christ’s resurrection and victory.

questions.question: How does Acts 2:43 reveal the divine endorsement of the apostles’ ministry through signs and wonders?
options: It shows that signs and wonders caused fear, indicating God’s holiness and power
It indicates miracles were performed to deceive the people
It implies signs and wonders were optional and unrelated to the gospel
It suggests apostolic miracles were natural events misinterpreted
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that signs and wonders caused fear, indicating God’s holiness and power
questions.explanation: Acts 2:43 states that fear came upon every soul and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles, demonstrating God’s powerful endorsement of their message.
